messages.content:
You tailor resume bullets to a job posting without changing what is true. You get facts about one experience, each with an id, and the bullets now on the resume. Rewrite each bullet for the posting and cite the facts it rests on.

Rules. A verifier checks them, and a bullet that breaks one is thrown away and replaced by the original, so do not push against them:
1. No new numbers. Every number must come from a fact you cite; do not add, combine or compute.
2. No new technologies, products or proper nouns that the cited facts or the tech list do not name.
3. No absolute words (never, always, guaranteed, zero, every, all, exactly-once, 100%) unless a cited fact says so.
4. No causes or mechanisms the facts do not state: "by X", "through X", "so that X" only where a fact links X to that result.
5. Round only the unflattering way: show a number as written or rounded down, never up (3,781 may become 3.7K+, never 3.8K+).
6. Use the posting's words only where they describe this work accurately.
Also: respect the "must not claim" list, keep each bullet to one sentence, start it with a past-tense verb, and put every fact you used in sources.
Return exactly as many bullets as you are asked for, in the order given.

Posting: Site Reliability Engineer at Basalt Wharf Cloud
Responsibilities:
- Own the availability targets for our core services: define service level objectives, track error budgets and decide with product teams when to slow down.
- Run and improve the Kubernetes clusters that host our services, including upgrades, capacity planning and autoscaling.
- Manage infrastructure as code with Terraform, and review changes from other teams for safety.
- Build monitoring and alerting with Prometheus and Grafana that points at causes instead of symptoms.
- Lead incident response, write blameless postmortems and follow the action items through.
- Automate toil in Python or Go and push the on-call load down quarter by quarter.
Requirements:
- Three or more years running production services on a major cloud, preferably AWS.
- Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, Linux and networking fundamentals.
- A record of reducing alert noise or incident counts that you can describe with numbers.
- Clear written communication: runbooks, postmortems and design notes.
Keywords:
- Site Reliability Engineer
- Basalt Wharf Cloud
- hosted scheduling platform
- availability targets

- error budgets

- networking fundamentals

- clear written communication
- runbooks
- service meshes
- chaos testing
- progressive delivery
- PostgreSQL operations
- backup and restore drills

Experience: Dispatch Desk: a tool-using claim-triage agent
Tech list: Python, Ollama, SQLite, pytest, Docker
Facts you may cite:
[dispatch-desk#1] Built a tool-using agent in Python that triages freight-damage claims with an 8B open-weights model served locally by Ollama and one retrieval tool over a SQLite table of 3,200 past claims.
[dispatch-desk#2] Passed 35 of 40 hand-written claim scenarios (0.875), against 22 of 40 (0.55) for the same model without the retrieval tool.
[dispatch-desk#3] Recorded every model call and tool call in a SQLite trace, so that a failing scenario replays offline in under 2 s.
[dispatch-desk#4] Wrote 58 pytest cases, 6 of them replaying recorded traces, and ran them in CI in 4 minutes.
[dispatch-desk#scope] ORIGIN: personal project, built to learn how tool calling fails. EVIDENCE: eval/results.json (40 scenarios written by the author, one run at temperature 0 with seed 9; a second run gave 34 of 40, 0.85); the agent called the retrieval tool in 37 of the 40 scenarios and no other model tool (the date parser and the currency formatter are plain functions that the model cannot call); the 3,200 past claims are synthetic; the replay time is the median of 20 replays on one laptop; CI time is from the last 10 runs.
Must not claim:
- a production model, a deployment or real users (it runs on one laptop and nothing was deployed)
- a multi-tool agent or 'three tools' (the retrieval tool is the only tool the model can call)
- 0.875 as a stable figure (a single run; a second run gave 0.85)
- accuracy on real claims (the claims are synthetic and the scenarios were written by the author)
- any comparison with other models (one 8B model only)

Bullets to rewrite (return exactly 2; bullet k is the rewrite of k):
1. Built a tool-using agent in Python that triages freight-damage claims with an 8B open-weights model served locally by Ollama and one retrieval tool over a SQLite table of 3,200 past claims.
2. Passed 35 of 40 hand-written claim scenarios (0.875), against 22 of 40 (0.55) for the same model without the retrieval tool.
